source.title: Well-posed infinite horizon variational problems on a compact manifold

accepted.question_text: How do the smooth solutions u_alpha of the discounted modified Hamilton-Jacobi equation H(du_alpha) - alpha u_alpha = constant change as alpha varies down to 0, the parameter value at which the corresponding standard Hamilton-Jacobi equation generally lacks smooth solutions and is understood only in a generalized sense? Here H is the natural mechanical Hamiltonian associated with the Riemannian kinetic energy and potential U, and alpha is the discount parameter in the infinite-horizon variational problem.

evidence.quote: Submanifold Ψ ⊂ T ∗M in Theorem 2 is the graph of an exact 1-form on M, i. e. Ψ = {dqu : q ∈ M}, where u is a C2-function on M. Then u is a solution of the modified Hamilton–Jacobi equation: H(du ) − αu = const.

Standard Hamilton–Jacobi equation corresponds to α = 0. As we know, in general, this equation does not have smooth solutions, it has only gen-eralized ones. It would be very interesting to study transformations of the solutions for the parameter α running from the indicated by Theorem 2 “smooth area” to 0.

accepted.question_text: Can smooth optimal synthesis for discounted infinite-horizon variational problems be developed for settings beyond compact Riemannian manifolds with a natural mechanical Hamiltonian, specifically for more general Lagrangians or for variational problems with nonholonomic constraints? The target notion is a well-posed infinite-horizon problem in which every initial state has a unique minimizing trajectory and the minimizers are generated by a smooth dynamical system.

evidence.quote: In this paper we assume that the manifold M is compact.
The Hamiltonian H is the energy of a natural mechanical system on the Riemannian manifold and the discount factor α plays the role of a negative friction coefficient.
This and other generalizations (more general Lagrangians, prob-lems with nonholonomic constraints) could be subjects of forthcoming pa-pers.
